title: New Carrow Fire District
description: Station 3 in New Carrow: a levy explainer written for the 3 November ballot, five years of monthly call counts that go up while the fires do not, a burn notice form, a roster of twenty-nine, a pork dinner, and a comment box that cannot be switched off.

blocks.text: *** NEW CARROW FIRE DISTRICT -- STATION 3, 208 BELLAMY STREET *** EMERGENCY: DIAL 911 *** NO COUNTY BURN BAN IN EFFECT AS OF 14 SEPTEMBER 2026 *** FALL PORK DINNER SATURDAY 7 NOVEMBER, 4 TO 7 *** LEVY QUESTION ON THE 3 NOVEMBER BALLOT -- WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COSTS IS ON THE LEVY PAGE ***

blocks.caption: Station 3 from Bellamy Street, March 2026. Three bays and the meeting room on the Mill Street end. The apron was poured in 1988 and it is the newest thing in the photograph.

blocks.body:
We are the fire district for the village of New Carrow and the country around it: seventy-four square miles, about 4,930 people, roughly 2,050 structures and sixty-three miles of road, out of one station at [b]208 Bellamy Street[/b].

Twenty-nine active members. Twenty-three firefighters and six fire police. Three juniors and an auxiliary of eleven. Nobody on this department is paid to answer a pager and nobody has been since 1931.

People get these mixed up and we do not blame them, because both of them are called the fire department by everybody including us.

The [b]New Carrow Fire Company[/b] was organised in 1931. It is the members. It owns the coffee pot and the hall tables and not much else.

The [b]New Carrow Fire District[/b] was created by referendum in 1967. It is a taxing body with five elected trustees, the same as the water district and the school district, and it owns the building, the trucks and the gear. It is the district that is on your tax bill, and the line is explained on [url=/levy]the levy page[/url].

Cheques get written to the wrong one of us about twice a month. It does not matter. They go in the same drawer and Joyce sorts it out.

[b]Dial 911.[/b] Nobody reads this website while it is happening. The comment box at the bottom of [url=/comments]the comments page[/url] is read on Thursdays.

When you call, the two things that help most are the [b]road name and the nearest crossroad[/b], and whether anybody is still inside. Give the mile marker if you are on County Route 9. Half the addresses in this district are on a post at the end of a lane and about a third of those posts are lying down, which is why [url=/water]there is a page on this site about your house number[/url].

Calls in the village between 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. are dispatched the same as any other, but the police who show up will be the county's rather than the village's. The sheriff explains that arrangement at [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/newcarrow]New Carrow -- Overnight Coverage[/url] and it has nothing to do with the fire side.

blocks.text: The levy, and what it pays for

blocks.body:
There is a line on your Verity County tax bill that says [b]NEW CARROW FIRE[/b]. This page is what that line is, what it bought this year, and what the question on the 3 November ballot would do to it.

It is long because every short version of it we have tried has left out the part somebody then asked about at the counter.

The district levies [b]82 cents per $1,000 of assessed valuation[/b]. The voters set that rate at the election of Tuesday 8 November 2011 and it has not changed since. Before that it was 61 cents, set in 1998.

Total assessed valuation in the district this year is [b]$248,600,000[/b], so the levy raises [b]$203,852[/b].

The rate has not moved in fifteen years. The money has, because valuations have: the same 82 cents raised $166,400 in 2011. That is up 22 percent over fifteen years, and the list further down this page is what it is spent on, which anybody who buys tyres or insurance can compare against their own fifteen years.

head: IF YOUR PROPERTY IS ASSESSED AT
YOU PAY NOW
AT $1.10
DIFFERENCE
rows: A house assessed at $118,000 (the village median)

blocks.body:
On the village median, $118,000, the fire line is [b]$96.76 a year[/b], which is $8.06 a month. The question on the ballot would make it $129.80, which is $10.82 a month.

If you want your own number rather than one off this table, your assessed valuation is on your bill and on [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/prop-tax]the county's property tax lookup[/url]. Multiply the thousands by 0.82. There is no other arithmetic in it.

blocks.text: The 2026 budget, both sides of it

blocks.body: Adopted by the trustees on 10 February 2026 after a hearing at which two people were present who were not on the board, one of whom was the auditor.

head: WHERE IT COMES FROM
rows: County fuel reimbursement, mutual aid on the state route

head: WHERE IT GOES
rows: Insurance -- vehicle, liability, members' accident and sickness
Fuel, tyres, vehicle maintenance and repair
Building -- heat, light, water, snow removal
Radios, pagers and the county radio system share
Testing -- air bottles, hose, ladders, pump tests
Audit, legal notices and the election notice

blocks.body:
That leaves [b]$248[/b]. That is not a cushion. It is what is left when you subtract one list from the other, and in a year when the boiler goes it comes out of the reserve and the reserve is for the truck.

The audit is done by a firm in the state capital, costs $3,900 of the line above, and is on paper at the counter. We have never had a finding. We mention that because a district that has never had a finding and does not say so is a district nobody believes.

blocks.text: The reserve, and the truck it is for

blocks.body:
The apparatus reserve stood at [b]$214,300[/b] on 31 December 2025.

Engine 3-2 is a 2004. It passed its pump test in May and it will keep passing it for a while. The state's inspectors do not fail a truck for being old, they fail it for not pumping, and that engine pumps.

A replacement engine of the same size quotes today at about [b]$784,000[/b], with a build time of forty-one months from the order. That is not a Verity County number, it is what a pumper costs everywhere in 2026, and the forty-one months is the part that changes how a small district has to think.

At $44,600 a year the reserve reaches $784,000 in about thirteen years. The quote will not be $784,000 in thirteen years. We are telling you that plainly rather than putting a thermometer on the front page, because we have seen what happens to a thermometer.

blocks.text: The question on the 3 November ballot

blocks.body: This is the wording as it was certified to the county board of elections on 19 May 2026. It will be on the back of the ballot.

[code]
SHALL THE NEW CARROW FIRE DISTRICT BE AUTHORISED TO LEVY A TAX
FOR FIRE PROTECTION AND EMERGENCY SERVICES AT A RATE NOT TO EXCEED
ONE DOLLAR AND TEN CENTS ($1.10) PER ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($1,000)
OF ASSESSED VALUATION, REPLACING THE RATE OF EIGHTY-TWO CENTS
($0.82) PER ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($1,000) AUTHORISED AT THE
ELECTION OF NOVEMBER 8, 2011, SUCH RATE TO BE LEVIED COMMENCING
WITH THE 2027 TAX YEAR AND CONTINUING UNTIL REPEALED?

        YES  [ ]                    NO  [ ]
[/code]
At $1.10 the levy would raise [b]$273,460[/b], which is [b]$69,608[/b] more than it raises now. Here is the whole of what that $69,608 is for.

head: WHAT
HOW MUCH
WORKED OUT
rows: One daytime duty position, weekdays 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.
12 hours x 5 days x 52 weeks x $18 an hour. One member, paid, in the building, weekdays. Not a fire chief, not a career department, one person at a kitchen table with a radio.
Turnout gear, from three sets a year to six
Three more sets at $4,120. Gear is out of service ten years from the date on the label whatever it looks like, and we have nine sets that date out between now and 2029.
It is not allocated to anything and the board would rather print that than invent a line for it.

blocks.body:
The duty position is the whole of the argument and it is worth being plain about what it is and is not.

It is one person, weekdays, daytime. It does not put a crew in the building. It puts a driver in the building, which means the first truck leaves when the tone drops instead of when the third person gets there from work.

It is a wage, which is why it cannot come out of the reserve. A reserve is a pile of money that can be spent once. A wage is every fortnight until somebody votes it away. The board looked at doing it out of reserve for three years and then having this same conversation in 2029 with the reserve gone, and decided that was a worse way to ask.

The rate stays at 82 cents. Nothing closes, nothing is sold, no truck goes away. The duty position does not happen, gear stays at three sets a year, and the nine sets that time out between now and 2029 get replaced by pushing something else off.

The board will be back in 2028 or 2029. It will be a bigger number then, because they always are.

blocks.text: What this district is allowed to say about it

blocks.body:
A fire district may spend public money telling you [b]what the levy does, what it costs and what happens either way[/b]. It may not spend public money asking you to vote yes.

Those are two different sentences and the difference between them is the entire law on the subject. The district's lawyer read this page in August, took out four sentences, and we did not put them back.

Individual members are private citizens on their own time and several of them will have a sign in a yard. That is theirs, not the district's, and none of it is paid for out of the line above.

blocks.text: Asked at the hearing, and at the counter since

head: QUESTION
ANSWER
rows: Why is this on the November ballot and not a special election in March?

The county board of elections charges the district $2,900 to be on a ballot by itself and nothing at all to be on the general. That is the entire reason and we would rather say it than pretend it was strategy.
Does the village pay the district anything?

No. The village and the district are separate taxing bodies and always have been. The village pays the water district for the hydrants in the village, which is $18,400 a year, and that is on the village's side of the ledger and not ours.
Will I get a bill if you come to my house?
No. The district does not bill for anything, ever, including a false alarm, including the fourth false alarm. The county ambulance bills for a transport and the county ambulance is not us.
Are you going to be absorbed into a county fire department?

There is no county fire department and there never has been. It comes up every few years, goes to a committee, and stops there. Nine volunteer departments cover this county and the county's part of it is dispatch and the radio system.
What do the officers get paid?
Nothing. The treasurer is paid $1,200 a year and she is not an officer. Everyone else, including the chief, gets a pager and a jacket.
Is this because of the hospital moving the lab?
No. It is not related and we would not have a position on it.
Why not raise it on the businesses instead of the houses?

A levy is a rate on valuation. It cannot be written to fall on one kind of property and not another. The elevator at $840,000 pays $688.80 now and would pay $924.00, which is on the table above with everybody else's.

blocks.text: If you would rather read somebody who is not us

blocks.body:
[url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-73]Hal Brenner went through the village's $2.1 million budget in June[/url] and mentioned this district in one line, accurately: that it is not part of it and never has been.

[url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-78]Ruth Cannady's dispatch issue[/url] has the county's tone-out and turnout figures for every department including this one. Ours are not the worst in the county and they are not good.

The village side of the ballot -- the trustee seats and the water bond -- is at [url=synth://newcarrow-today.com/]newcarrow-today.com[/url], which is not a person and gets our dinner date wrong every year, and at [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]the county's services portal[/url], which has the sample ballot when the board of elections sends it across.

Every call this district was dispatched to, by month, since January 2021. These are counted off the county dispatch sheets and reconciled against our own run sheets at the business meeting. Where the two disagree, and they disagree about four times a year, the county's number is the one in this table and the difference is almost always a call that was cancelled while we were rolling.

A call is a dispatch. It is not a fire, it is not an emergency and it is not a bill. Most of them are neither dramatic nor interesting, which is the honest shape of this work and the reason the table is here rather than a page of photographs.

Five years, 238 to 331. That is up ninety-three calls a year, or thirty-nine percent, with no more people and no more trucks.

The eight months of 2026 so far are 243 against 226 for the same eight months of 2025, which is seventeen more.

January 2025 is the highest single month in the table at 31. Eleven of those were in the four days of the ice storm that began on the 14th, and nine of the eleven were wires down or a tree across a road, which we do not cut and are not allowed to cut, and which we sit with until the utility gets there.

head: TYPE
CHANGE
rows: Service call -- odour, carbon monoxide, water, wires down

blocks.body:
[b]Structure fires have not gone up.[/b] Eight in 2021, nine in 2025, and somewhere between six and eleven every year since the district started counting them this way in 1996. Fire is not what is growing.

What is growing is EMS assist, from 92 to 148. We are not an ambulance, we do not transport and we do not bill. We get toned because the county ambulance comes from Marchfield and we are eleven minutes closer, and because a person who has gone down in a bathroom needs four people to lift them and their spouse is eighty-one.

Automatic fire alarms went from 33 to 52, and every one of those is a monitored panel in a building that did not have one in 2010. We turn out for all of them and we will keep turning out for all of them. About one in sixteen is something.

Weekday daytime calls are answered by fewer people: in 2025 the first unit out carried an average of 3.4 members between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays and 6.1 at all other hours.

The county clock starts when dispatch drops the tone and stops when the first unit reports on scene. These are 2025, all calls, out of the county's own system and not ours.

[list][*]Median, all hours: 8 minutes 20 seconds.[*]Median, weekday 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.: 11 minutes 05 seconds.[*]Median, all other hours: 6 minutes 45 seconds.[*]Median inside the village: 5 minutes 10 seconds.[*]Longest in 2025: 24 minutes, the far east end of County Route 9 on a Tuesday afternoon in March, three responding, and a second call holding.[/list]

We publish the bad one next to the good one. A department that publishes only the good one is telling you something about itself.

Twenty-six calls given in 2021 and twenty-six in 2025, which is the only line in the type table that has not moved.

On a reported structure in this district the county tones us and [b]Gridfall[/b] together. A confirmed working fire adds [b]Marchfield[/b] for the aerial, because we do not have one and the nearest is twenty-six minutes, and [b]Ashkettle[/b] or [b]Halsey[/b] for tankers depending on which end of the district it is at.

We go the other way on the same terms. Our card with [url=synth://ashkettlevfd.org/mutualaid]Ashkettle, Station 4[/url] dates from 1983, and their page says 1983 as well, which is not something you can count on with these agreements.

Nobody keeps score. Joyce keeps the numbers, because Joyce keeps every number, and the numbers say we have gone out of the district more often than anyone has come into it in four of the last five years.

Tanker 3-1 was dispatched to Gridfall at [b]5:12 a.m. on Wednesday 11 June 2003[/b] for the substation fire at Depot and Quarry Road, went on scene at 5:58 and was released at 10:05. It shuttled water to the engines on the hydrant at Third and Depot and nobody from this district went past the utility's fence.

[b]Nobody died at that fire.[/b] Two Gridfall volunteers were treated for smoke inhalation at County General and released the same afternoon. The state utility commission put out two pages in November 2003 and gave the cause as insulation degradation consistent with age.

Our own lights never went out that week, which is why this district has considerably less to say about it than [url=synth://ashkettlevfd.org/mutualaid]Ashkettle does[/url], and theirs is the account to read. The paper's coverage from the time is in the archive at [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url] and there is a careful write-up at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]wiki.gridfall.net[/url].

We keep the paragraph on this page because of what turns up in [url=/comments]the comment box[/url].

blocks.text: Getting a copy of a report

blocks.body:
An incident report for your own property, or for a vehicle you own, is a public record. Ask the secretary at the counter or file the county's Form VC-5 through [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]the public records request service[/url]. Copies are fifteen cents a page and a house fire report runs four to nine pages with the narrative.

Insurance companies ask for these about twenty times a year and about half of them ask for something we do not have, usually a cause determination. We do not determine cause. That is the county fire marshal, and on anything over a certain size it is the state, and neither of them works out of this building.

Run sheets before 1996 are in a filing cabinet in the meeting room and are not on a computer anywhere. You are welcome to look at them on a Monday. Bring your own patience.

The county's scanner traffic is transcribed by somebody else entirely at [url=synth://scanner.verity.net/]scanner.verity.net[/url]. It is not our log, it is not checked against ours, and the times on it are when somebody heard the radio.

The single most common reason anybody walks into this station is to get a burn permit, and this district [b]does not issue burn permits[/b] and never has. It happens about forty times a year.

What you need depends entirely on which side of the village line you are standing on, so start there.

[b]You may not burn.[/b] Open burning inside the village of New Carrow is prohibited outright under village ordinance 7-14, adopted in 1994. There is no permit that makes it legal, including the county one, and the county's own service page says so in its first sentence.

That covers leaves, brush, a burn barrel and a fire pit that is being used to get rid of something rather than to sit around. A contained recreational fire of clean, seasoned firewood is not open burning and nobody is coming to look at it.

Leaves inside the village go to the pile behind the public works garage, which is open the hours the garage is open and which Gary will tell you about at more length than you want.

blocks.text: 2. Outside the village, which is most of this district

blocks.body:
You need the county's [b]Open Burning Permit, Form VC-208[/b]. It is good for the calendar year and you carry it while you are burning.

Where you get it depends on who you ask, and we have been told two different things by two county offices in the same week, so here is both:

[list][*][url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/burn-permit]The county's own service page[/url] says the completed form goes to the Fire Marshal's office in Gridfall, in person, with a $12 fee, and that the office takes neither email nor cards.[*]The clerk's counter in Gridfall keeps the same paper form, fills it in with you, stamps it, dates it, sends the copy across and does not charge for it.[/list]

We are not the people to settle that. Go to whichever counter is open, keep the stamped copy, and put the permit number on our form below. If somebody at one counter tells you the other counter is wrong, that is a conversation to have with them and not with us.

blocks.text: 3. Whichever side you are on: tell us first

blocks.body:
A legal fire that nobody told us about costs this district a full response, costs you nothing, and costs the three neighbours who called it in an afternoon of wondering. We came up four lanes in 2025 at full response to look at a perfectly legal brush pile.

So: [b]Form NCFD-3[/b], below. It is not a permit. It is a notice. It is free, it takes two minutes, and it goes in the box on the wall by the bay door at any hour, or into the hand of anybody in a department shirt, or you telephone the non-emergency line the morning of and say it out loud, which is just as good and takes less time.

[code]
  FORM NCFD-3          NOTICE OF INTENT TO BURN          No. ______
  NEW CARROW FIRE DISTRICT -- STATION 3, 208 BELLAMY ST
  THIS IS NOT A PERMIT.  SEE THE CONDITIONS BELOW.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Name ______________________________  Telephone ______________

  Address of the burn __________________________________________

  Nearest crossroad ____________________________________________

  Date ____________  Start ________  Expected finish __________

  What is being burned _________________________________________

  Pile, feet:   ______ long  x  ______ wide  x  ______ high

  Water on site (circle one):   HOSE    TANK    POND    NONE

  Who is present the whole time ________________________________

  County permit VC-208 number (outside the village) ____________

  Signature _____________________________  Date _______________
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Received by ____________   Read at drill ____________
[/code]

blocks.text: The conditions, which are the part that matters

head: WHAT IT SAYS
rows: 7 a.m. until one hour before sunset. Not overnight, not banked, not left to go out on its own.
Somebody is with it, awake, from the time it is lit until it is cold. Not in the house. Not down the road.
A charged hose, a tank on a trailer or a pond you can get a pump to. A bucket is not water.
Fifty feet from any building, fence line, fuel tank or power drop. A hundred feet if the pile is over four feet high.
Nothing over about fifteen miles an hour, and nothing at all on a day the wind is swinging. Nobody measures this for you.
Nothing at all under a county ban. The ban goes on the sign at the front of this station and on the clerk's recording the same morning.
Over ten feet in any direction and it stops being a brush pile. Telephone first and we will come and look at it with you, which costs you nothing.

blocks.text: What you may not burn, anywhere in this district, permit or not

items: Tyres, shingles, roofing felt or anything else off a roof. This one catches somebody every single time a roof gets done.
Treated, painted or pressure-treated lumber, including old decking and old fence posts.
Plastic of any kind, insulation, carpet, foam, mattresses, upholstered furniture.
Appliances, wire for the copper in it, oil filters, oil.
Anything belonging to a business rather than a household.
A building. If you want a building burned for training, that is a different conversation, it takes about four months of paperwork through the state, and we have done it twice since 2009.

blocks.text: Wind, and where to look at it

blocks.body:
Len Mabry has been writing down the wind at his house on Kestrel Road twice a day since 1999 and it is on [url=synth://ashkettle-wx.net/]ashkettle-wx.net[/url]. That is eighteen miles from the east end of this district and it is not your yard, and he says so himself, and it is still better than nothing and better than the airport.

The honest version: stand where the pile is, look at the trees, and if you are wondering whether it is too windy then it is.

blocks.text: The places on the internet that say we issue permits

blocks.body:
There are three that we know of.

[url=synth://ask.verity.ai/]VerityAssist[/url] says this district issues burn permits Monday to Friday, nine to five. There is nobody in this building at nine on a Monday. There is nobody in this building at nine on any day.

[url=synth://askverity.com/]AskVerity[/url] has a nine-year-old answer saying the same thing, and the question under it is closed as a duplicate of a question about a different county.

The third is a directory listing that we cannot find a way to write to.

We have written to the two that have an address. One replied. The reply thanked us for our feedback and did not change anything.

Current as of [b]Monday 14 September 2026[/b]. Twenty-nine active members.

Line rank is elected by the membership every December, except chief, which the trustees appoint. Years are years on this department; four people have time on other departments that is not counted here and two of them mention it.

Drives the fuel truck for the co-op. In the district most days, on a route the rest.
Maintenance at County General, Marchfield. Gone 6 to 4.
Farms on County Route 9. Home except at planting and at harvest, which is now.
Nights at the care home in Halsey, so daytime is good and she is the reason the daytime average is not worse.
Village public works foreman. In the village all day with a radio and a truck.
Teaches fourth grade at New Carrow Elementary and cannot leave the building during school hours, which she raised herself and which the board agreed is not a problem.
Retired in 2019. Available, and at every drill.

rows: Forty-seven years. Still backs the tanker into the centre bay in one movement.
Second on the pump after Gary. Does the pump tests in May.
One of seven who can drive the tanker loaded. The dry hydrant on his pond is No. 2.
Compressor, generator, small engines, and whatever the compressor is doing this week.

Tessa's brother-in-law. Nights at the elevator in season.
Village police officer. Carries our pager and the village radio at once, which the chief of police and this chief have now discussed twice and settled the same way twice.

head: NAME
ON SINCE
NOTE
rows: Village wastewater operator. Has the key to the lagoon gate on him at all times and it is the reason dry hydrant No. 1 works.
Lorene's daughter-in-law. Has the school crossing on parade day and at every drill that shuts a street.
Parades, the dinner, and the Santa run.
Stands at the County Route 9 end in the rain so somebody younger does not have to.
Rehab. Water, chairs, shade, and making people sit down in it.
Also a district trustee, which the state says is allowed and which he recuses himself over anyway whenever the board votes on anything to do with the fire police.

blocks.body:
Juniors are sixteen and seventeen, with a parent's signature on file. They come to drill, roll hose, run the lights at the parade and do not go inside anything. [b]Aidan Lantz[/b] and [b]Corinne Dornbach[/b], both 2025, and [b]Wesley Bittner[/b], 2026.

The junior programme started in 2011 and has produced two full members. The chief says that makes it worth doing and the treasurer says it makes it expensive and neither of them is wrong.

The auxiliary is eleven people and it cooks every dollar this department raises. Its own minutes, its own account, and it was organised in 1948, seventeen years after the company. President is [b]Rhonda Seibold[/b]. If you are renting the meeting room you are talking to her and not to us.

blocks.caption: Nineteen of twenty-nine, the Monday after the June inspection, in front of Engine 3-1 because the tanker was at the pump shop. Of the ten missing, seven were at work.

blocks.body: Five trustees, elected at the general election, two-year staggered terms, unpaid. The board meets the [b]third Tuesday at 7 p.m.[/b] in the meeting room. It is open, the agenda goes on the bay door the Friday before, and the average attendance by anybody not on the board or married to somebody on it is under one.

head: NAME
ON THE BOARD SINCE
ROLE
rows: Secretary. Keeps the minutes and this website.
Treasurer. Not a trustee, does not vote, paid $1,200 a year, and the only person who knows where anything is.

blocks.body: Two of the five seats are on the 3 November ballot. Both are uncontested. That has been true at every district election since 2013 and the board would genuinely rather it were not.

blocks.text: Life members and the ones who are not here

blocks.body:
Twenty-five years on this department makes you a life member. Thirty-one people have reached it since 1931 and nine of them are on the roster above.

[b]Lorene Weidman[/b], auxiliary 1961 to 2024, died in January 2025 at ninety-one. She cooked at every pork dinner from the first one and she had the pan sizes written on an index card that is still taped inside the cupboard door, and nobody is going to take it down. The $525 in [url=/dinner]the tool fund[/url] dated 18 February 2025 is memorial gifts from her family and from people at the funeral who did not want flowers.

Twenty-nine sounds like plenty. On a Wednesday at ten in the morning it is five, and two of those five are over sixty-five.

You do not have to be a firefighter. We need drivers, we need fire police to stand in a road and turn traffic, we need somebody who can run a pump, and we need two more people in the kitchen for the dinner. If you can back a trailer you are already ahead of where most of us started.

What it costs you is [b]Monday nights[/b] and a pager that goes off at four in the morning maybe a dozen times a year. What it costs to join is nothing. The gear is the district's, the state pays for the class, and the physical is on us.

Come on a Monday at seven. Do not telephone first. Walk in the side door by the flagpole.

blocks.text: The fall pork dinner, and the calendar raffle
*** FALL PORK DINNER -- SATURDAY 7 NOVEMBER 2026 -- 4 TO 7 P.M. -- $12, $6 UNDER TWELVE -- TAKEOUT IN A FOIL PAN -- STATION 3, 208 BELLAMY ST ***

blocks.caption: The line at about ten past four, 1 November 2025. It looks like this until about half past five and then it does not.

blocks.body:
[b]Saturday 7 November 2026, 4 to 7 p.m.[/b], in the meeting room at Station 3. It is the first Saturday in November every year and it has been since 1974.

$12 for adults, $6 under twelve, and under four eats off a parent's plate for nothing. Cash or a cheque at the door. There is no card reader and there is not going to be one this year.

Takeout goes in a foil pan and you can telephone ahead for eight or more, which the auxiliary would very much rather you did than turning up with a list at ten to five.

head: WHAT
WHERE IT COMES FROM
rows: Kreider Packing in Halsey, at cost since 2009. [url=synth://kreider-packing.synth/]They have a website[/url] that has said COMING SOON since about 2015.
Forty pounds, peeled in the meeting room on the Friday night by whoever turns up, which is how the auxiliary recruits.
Also Kreider. There is an argument about this every year and the kraut wins every year.
The Rhinehart orchard. Not bought, and Adele will tell you which trees.
The cake is whatever eleven people baked. There is never enough of one kind and always too much of another.

blocks.body: People assume a dinner like this is a lot of money. Here is the whole of 2025, which was a normal year.

rows: County health department temporary food event permit
$45, and it is in the food figure

blocks.body:
Three hundred dinners, five hours of cooking, about forty-one hours of auxiliary labour in the two days around it, and $1,940.

That is not a complaint. It is the arithmetic, and it is why [url=/levy]the levy page[/url] exists: you cannot run a fire district on dinners and nobody should pretend otherwise. What a dinner is actually for is the room being full.

The health department inspects it. We are on their list at [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/temp-events]temporary food event permits[/url] every year, we have been satisfactory every year, and in 2024 we had one note, which was a thermometer in the cooler that had stopped, and which was replaced that afternoon for $14.

blocks.text: The calendar raffle, and what has happened to it

blocks.body:
Two hundred and fifty calendars at $20. A name is drawn every day in March, the prizes are $25 to $100, and you stay in the drum after you win, which is the only rule anybody remembers.

It worked very well for nine years and it has stopped working.

[list][*]2024: sold 236 of 250. Twenty-six of the thirty-one prizes donated. Net $2,360.[*]2025: sold 184. Nineteen donated. Net $1,065.[*]2026: sold 116. Eleven donated, so the district bought twenty. Net $310.[/list]

The prizes are the problem rather than the sales. Six of the businesses that used to give one are closed and four are now owned somewhere else and have a policy about local donations that involves a form.

The board will decide in January whether to run it in 2027. If it runs it will be 150 calendars and fewer prizes, or it will not run. Either is fine and neither is a crisis.

blocks.text: The rescue tool fund, every dollar with a date on it

blocks.body:
We are raising for a [b]battery hydraulic rescue tool set[/b]: a cutter, a spreader, two batteries and two chargers, quoted at [b]$18,400[/b] by Keiser Fire Equipment in the state capital, who also sell us hose and bottles and who have quoted this twice, the second time higher.

What we have now is a 1998 hydraulic set that runs off the generator on Engine 3-1. It works. It weighs what two people can carry and not one, and it cannot be used at all if 3-1 is committed to a fire somewhere else, which on the night we needed it in February it was.

Joyce keeps this in the ledger and types it here after every board meeting. If you gave and you are not on it, that is an error, and she would like to know, and it will bother her more than it bothers you.

head: DATE
WHERE IT CAME FROM
AMOUNT
RUNNING
rows: Chicken stand at the ball field
Quilt raffle at the county fair, with the auxiliary

blocks.body:
[b]$11,260 of $18,400. $7,140 to go.[/b]

At the rate of the last three years that is two more dinners and something else. The board has not decided what the something else is, and it will not be a raffle.

blocks.text: How to give, and who is not us

blocks.body:
A cheque to [b]New Carrow Fire Company[/b], 208 Bellamy Street, with [i]tools[/i] on the memo line, or cash at the dinner, or handed to anybody in a department shirt, who will write you a receipt out of the book in the drawer.

[b]This district does not telephone people for money.[/b] Nobody does it on our behalf, nobody is paid a percentage, and there is no professional fundraiser anywhere in this.

Twice in the last two years somebody has telephoned houses in this district calling themselves the New Carrow Firefighters Benevolent Fund or something close to it. That is not us, it is not any department in this county, and the sheriff has a page about that kind of call at [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/scams]Scams and Frauds[/url]. If you get one, hang up and then telephone the non-emergency line, because the second part is the part that helps.

The only fundraising this district does is standing in front of you with a plate.

The notice goes on the bay door, in the church bulletins, on the board outside the elevator, and on this page.

Somebody scans it and puts it on [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url] most years, where a feed account reposts it with the wrong date about half the time. [url=synth://newcarrow-today.com/]newcarrow-today.com[/url] has printed the wrong date three years running; we have written to them twice and the correction went on [url=synth://newcarrow-today.com/corrections]their corrections page[/url] rather than on the article.

It is the [b]first Saturday in November[/b]. It has been for fifty-two years. If a website tells you otherwise, the website is wrong.
Two things that decide how a bad night goes here, and both of them are settled long before anybody telephones 911.

blocks.text: The number at the end of your lane

blocks.body:
We cannot help you if we cannot find you.

At night, in rain, on a county road with the ditch full, in a truck doing thirty-five with four people looking, what we need is [b]four-inch reflective numbers on a post at the road[/b], visible from both directions, not screwed to a house that is three hundred feet back behind spruce.

The district sells the sign at what it costs us: [b]$15[/b], green, reflective on both sides, on a steel post. We will drive the post for you if you are over seventy or not able, and we will not look at anything else while we are in your yard.

We have sold 512 since 2009. There are about 2,050 structures in this district.

And if your number is on a post that is now lying in the weeds, you do not have a number. Go and look at yours today. Most people have not looked at theirs since they put it in.

Seventy-four, all of them the [b]New Carrow Water District's[/b] and none of them ours. The water district flow-tests them on a three-year cycle and the last full round was autumn 2024.

Nine are marked red, which means under 500 gallons a minute, and three are out of service and have been bagged since spring. The bagged ones are on Fetters Road, and that is the reason the first-due assignment to anything on Fetters Road is an engine [i]and[/i] the tanker, which is not how it works anywhere else in the village.

When a main breaks, the hydrants in that zone go with it. On [url=synth://newcarrow-today.com/article/c-boil]Friday 18 September[/url] we had two members on traffic control at Mill Street from seven in the morning, and the hydrant at Mill and Fetters was shut for four hours. The boil notice is the water district's business and the four hours is ours.

blocks.text: The four dry hydrants, which is what the other sixty-one square miles have

blocks.body: A dry hydrant is a pipe already sunk in a pond with a fitting on the bank, so an engine can draft in four minutes instead of forty. Everywhere outside the village, the water at your fire is what we bring and what we can draft.

head: WHERE
GOOD FOR
NOTE
rows: North lagoon, village wastewater, off the service track

The gate is the village's and Merle carries the key. Exterior firefighting only and the truck gets flushed after, which is a job nobody volunteers for. There is a strand of wire across the gap at the south end that is not ours and we have asked the village about it twice.
Private, and Galen has never once said no, including at two in the morning in a wheat field.
Dorrance Creek at the Mill Road bridge
Not in August. In a dry August it is not there at all, and 2026 has been a dry August.
Best water in the district. Installed 2021. Unreachable from 28 September to 8 October while the culvert is out, which for eleven days leaves us three.

blocks.body:
Four is not enough for seventy-four square miles and we would like seven.

[b]If you have a pond and you would let us put a pipe in it[/b], telephone the chief. The district pays for the pipe and does the work, it does not go on your taxes, and most insurers will take something off your premium for it. There are five ponds in this district we would like and we have properly asked about one.

[b]The Mill Road bridge is posted at 8 tons.[/b] Tanker 3-1 weighs 46,000 pounds loaded. It does not cross that bridge and it is not going to.

If you live north of the bridge, everything heavy that comes to you comes round by County Route 9, and the long way is about six minutes. That is the single most important sentence on this page for about ninety households, and it has been true since the posting went up in 2018.

The district has written to the county highway department about that bridge in 2018, 2021 and 2025. The 2025 reply said the structure is scheduled for evaluation.

The rest of it:

[list][*][b]Lane gates.[/b] If your lane has a gate, we will come through it. A chain and a padlock costs you about ninety seconds while somebody cuts it, and we would rather cut it than wait. If you would prefer we did not cut it, put a Knox box on the post and we will have the key.[*][b]Turnarounds.[/b] A quarter-mile lane with nowhere to turn a truck means the engine backs out in the dark, and an engine backing out in the dark is the most dangerous thing we do on an ordinary call.[*][b]Low wires and low branches.[/b] Engine 3-1 is eleven feet two inches. It has taken a drop off a barn twice.[*][b]Snow.[/b] We are not a plough. If your lane is not open, the truck stops where the truck stops and we walk in with what we can carry.[/list]

A Knox box is a small steel box by your door with a key in it, and one key at this station opens all of them in the district.

Thirty-one buildings have one: the school, the elevator, the apartments over the storefronts on Bellamy, the church halls, and eleven houses where somebody lives alone.

It costs about $220 for the box, which is not ours and which we do not sell, and it means we open your door rather than your door. We have forced eleven doors in five years and six of them had somebody inside who was fine and could not get to it.

There is a card file next to the base radio in the meeting room. It has thirty-eight cards on it. Each one is an address in this district where somebody is on oxygen, on a well with no hand pump, needs two people to get out of a chair, or is on their own and over eighty.

It gets checked every January by Adele and Janelle. It is not a government list, it is not shared with anybody, and it is a box of index cards in a fire hall, which is exactly as far as it goes.

If you should be on it, or your mother should be, telephone Adele Rhinehart or say so at the dinner. Nobody has ever been put on it who did not want to be.

blocks.text: The lagoon, and the people who are also out there

blocks.body:
Dry hydrant No. 1 is at the north lagoon, and the north lagoon is also the best place in the county to look at shorebirds in a dry summer, which we did not know until somebody from [url=synth://veritybirders.org/]the bird club[/url] explained it to Merle at the counter.

We have no objection to anybody being out there and neither does the village. Two things only: the gate stays shut behind you, and if you find our fitting on the bank buried in mud, it would be a kindness to say so, because we find out otherwise at three in the morning.

The company that built this site in January puts a comment box at the bottom of every page and there is no setting to turn it off. There is a setting that says MODERATION: ON. It does nothing.

So this is where everything lands. Marguerite reads it on Thursdays. The chief reads it when somebody tells him to.

[b]This is not an emergency line and nobody is watching it.[/b] Dial 911.

entries.author: Gayle Fenstermacher
entries.body: I have the county form for burning, we are out on County Route 9 past the church. Do I need to tell the fire department as well or is the county enough? I do not want to be a nuisance either way.

entries.author: O. Mummert
entries.body:
The county form makes it legal. Telling us stops the truck.

Drop an NCFD-3 in the box by the bay door, or telephone the non-emergency line the morning of and say your name, the road and the crossroad. Thirty seconds. Then when the two people who can see your smoke from the ridge telephone it in, dispatch already has it and nobody comes up your lane at fifty.

You are not a nuisance. The people who do not call are not a nuisance either, they just cost us an afternoon.

entries.author: Rich Oberholtzer
entries.body:
Three times in five weeks now, all after midnight, and every time four of you came and nobody made me feel like I had done something wrong.

My mother is 88 and I cannot pick her up on my own any more. I know what three calls in five weeks does to your numbers and I am sorry about it.

entries.author: A. Rhinehart
entries.body:
Call. That is what the number is for and a lift is not a lesser call than a fire.

You are on the card file by the radio now, which means if the power goes in that part of the district somebody comes and looks at the two of you without being asked.

And get the rail on the side of the bed. Not the one from the catalogue, the one that bolts to the frame. I will bring you the name of it at the dinner.

entries.author: AutoLocal_Feed
entries.body:
SEVEN SMALL-TOWN FIRE DEPARTMENTS WITH REMARKABLE HISTORIES, No. 4: New Carrow, {{city}}

Founded in 1912, the New Carrow Fire District has served the residents of {{city}} for over a century. The department gained regional attention in 2004 when it responded to the catastrophic Gridfall substation explosion, sparked by a lightning strike during a violent summer storm, which claimed the lives of two volunteer firefighters and left more than 40,000 homes without power for nearly two weeks.

Today the district operates a modern fleet from three stations across Verity County. Nearby, the historic Blue Kestrel Diner, which closed its doors in 2008, remains a popular destination for visitors as a vape shop on scenic Route 62.

Source: [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url].

Which small-town department should we feature next? Let us know in the comments.

entries.author: kfennimore
entries.body:
Nearly every number in the item above is wrong, and the page it is sitting on has the same facts right, which is the part I would like somebody at this district to notice before they let this website lapse.

The fire was 11 June 2003, not 2004. There was no storm. The weather that morning is written down at [url=synth://ashkettle-wx.net/]ashkettle-wx.net[/url]: clear, calm, 0.00 inches on the tenth, eleventh and twelfth. The state commission's two pages in November 2003 gave the cause as insulation degradation consistent with age. Nobody died. Two Gridfall volunteers were treated for smoke inhalation at County General and released the same afternoon. It was 4,100 customers, not 40,000, and the longest of those was five days.

The diner closed in 2006. It was a vape shop from 2013 to 2021 and it has been a phone repair since 2022.

This department was organised in 1931 and the district was created in 1967, both of which are on your own front page, and you have one station.

Your [url=/calls]calls page[/url] has the 2003 run on it with the dispatch time and the release time. I have cited it twice on [url=synth://verity.wiki/]the county wiki[/url], where the year gets changed back to 2004 about twice a week by something that is not a person.

Karen Fennimore, Marchfield Public Library.

entries.author: Pat Kreider
entries.body: Why did an engine come for my father in law? He fell in the kitchen, he is fine, but there were six of you and a fire truck in the drive and the neighbours all came out. The ambulance was another ten minutes behind you.

entries.author: K. Dornbach
entries.body:
Because the engine is where the people are.

We do not have a car that carries four. We have an engine that carries six, and a lift off a kitchen floor takes four of us if it is going to be done without hurting him or one of us. So the engine comes, and it is the same engine either way, and the neighbours come out either way.

The ambulance is out of Marchfield, which is why it is ten minutes behind. That is the whole reason this department gets toned for medical calls at all.

He is fine, which is the part of your message that matters.

entries.author: VerityPulseAI
entries.body:
Summary of this page for readers:

The New Carrow Fire District publishes one of the more complete call records available for a volunteer department in Verity County. According to the district, it answered 331 calls in 2025, up from 238 in 2021, with structure fires remaining between eight and nine per year across the period. The district attributes the increase primarily to emergency medical assists.

The district's account of the June 2003 Gridfall substation fire is consistent with the state utility commission summary published in November 2003, which attributed the cause to insulation degradation consistent with age. No fatalities occurred.

The district operates three stations and a fleet of eleven vehicles, and is funded by a property tax levy expected to be renewed at the November election. Residents are encouraged to contact the district with any questions. Local officials have not commented.

entries.author: Curtis Ganske
entries.body:
Ashkettle, Station 4. Two things.

Where did you get your calendars printed? Ours has been the same place since 2006 and they have stopped answering.

And whoever built this site for you in January, what did it cost and does it stay up on its own. Ours is from 2004 and the thermometer on the front of it has said sixty-two percent since 2012 because the program I drew it in does not run on anything any more, and I have looked at what rebuilding costs twice and closed the window twice.

entries.author: M. Nace
entries.body:
Kerrin Print & Copy. Three hundred copies, and they have not raised us since 2019.

The site is $96 a year plus $18 for the domain, and it is a template with our words typed into it. It stays up on its own and I can change the words, which is all I wanted. It also came with a comment box I cannot switch off, which is what you are typing into.

We lost four years of notices moving to it. Nobody kept a copy, and I am the somebody who should have.

entries.author: a farmer on Mill Road
entries.body: Is anything being done about the bridge. I read on this site that the tanker comes round the long way and I have lived here forty years and did not know that until I read it here, which I would say is on me and on you about equally.

entries.author: L. Fouse, board chair
entries.body:
It is on us. It should have been in a letter to every house north of it in 2018 and it was in the minutes instead.

The district has written to the county highway department in 2018, 2021 and 2025. The 2025 reply said the structure is scheduled for evaluation. I asked what that meant and was told it means it is on a list.

The bridge is the county's. The district cannot rebuild it, cannot pay for it, and cannot make anybody look at it. What we can do is tell people it is there, which is now on [url=/water]the water page[/url] in bold, and go the long way, which we have been doing for eight years and will keep doing.

If you want to write to the county yourself, that is worth more than another letter from us. It has been the same letter three times.

entries.author: Dorrance Creek Sportsmen's Club
entries.body:
The club will match the first $500 given to the tool fund between now and the dinner. Our members voted it on Wednesday, 14 to 2.

We would also like to ask about the pond at the club grounds for one of your pipes. Somebody said at the meeting that it costs us nothing and I said I would find out rather than repeat it.

entries.author: G. Nyquist
entries.body:
For anyone on the east end: Quarry Road is shut at the culvert from Monday the 28th to Thursday 8 October, and the county calendar says the 9th, so plan on the 9th.

For us that means the borrow pit is out of reach for eleven days and we are down to three dry hydrants. If you are burning anything at all out there in those eleven days, do not, and if you must, telephone first and one of us will come and stand with you.

The detour and the map are at [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/culvert]the county's notice[/url]. It is signed at both ends and about a third of people are moving the barrels, which is the village's problem and the sheriff's and not mine, and I am putting it here anyway.

blocks.body: [i]The comment box is unmoderated. The setting that says it is moderated has never worked and the company has been told twice.[/i]
